decisions.status_source: Re-homed 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 specification-completion pass): formerly recorded only at OPEN_ITEMS.md:123 (open_items/OI-176 and OI-177, PROTOCOL RATIFIED 2026-07-19, protocols in `cowork_prefit_gates.md`). The standing principle is CLAUDE.md #20. OPEN_ITEMS OI-237 closes on this move
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` #20: no value is graded on data that helped fit it, so the split and the capacity budget are declared BEFORE fitting and the headline claim is the held-out figure; a fitted-and-self-measured number is not established (#19). The ratified protocols are open_items/OI-176 (5-fold cross-validation grouped by ground-truth file) and OI-177 (parameter inventory, cell own-estimate only at count >= 20, <= 12 weights).

decisions.title: The exact-decode reserve - the declared prune was never adopted
decisions.verbatim:
**(c) The decode is EXACT; the declared reserve prune was never adopted, and what the decoder does narrow
has no specified form.** Exact semi-Markov Viterbi over the joint state is the ratified search. A prune was
decisions.plain: The estimator was meant to be allowed to narrow its search when that gets too slow. The narrowing rule that was specified turned out to cost more than it saved, so the estimator still searches exactly - and how it actually narrows in practice was never specified.
decisions.status_source: Re-homed 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 specification-completion pass): formerly recorded only at OPEN_ITEMS.md:211 (open_items/OI-188, OPEN - 'bounds every ceiling claim'); the admission rule actually in production still has no ratified basis (open_items/OI-226). OPEN_ITEMS OI-237 closes on this move
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `cowork_joint_estimator_factorization.md:170-173`: exact decode is expected tractable at chorale-scale event counts, and the reserve prune is an inference technique requiring its own established-loss measurement, never a silent heuristic. What the decoder actually prunes has no recorded derivation at all (open_items/OI-226).

decisions.title: Negative evidence is information - a ruled-out possibility is carried, not dropped
decisions.verbatim:
**Negative evidence is information — a ruled-out reading is carried, not dropped.** A layer that
eliminates a reading publishes the elimination rather than discarding it: the ruled-out reading is
carried on the output surface at low confidence, unless the elimination is recomputable from what that
decisions.plain: Knowing that something is not the case is itself useful. A reading that has been ruled out is kept at low confidence rather than thrown away, unless we could work out the exclusion again from what we did keep.
decisions.status_source: Re-homed 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 specification-completion pass): CLAUDE.md guiding principle #12, ratified by the user 2026-07-06, remains the standing principle; the layer-facing rule is now stated in the cross-cutting analysis contracts it governs. OPEN_ITEMS OI-237 closes on this move
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` #12: a ruled-out possibility is evidence - finding by exclusion - so it is carried at low confidence unless the exclusion is recomputable from what is kept.

decisions.title: Every derived fact is published exactly once, on the producing layer's output surface
decisions.verbatim:
**Every derived analytical fact is published exactly once, on the producing layer's output surface;
consumers read it and never re-derive it.** For **evidence-class** facts — hints a later design could
decisions.plain: Whatever a stage works out, it publishes on its own output surface; every later stage reads that instead of working it out again. Facts that are hints a later stage might one day use are published broadly even when nothing reads them yet, each carrying whether it has been established, because a consumer may not rely on an unestablished fact. What to do with a fact nobody reads is decided case by case: keep it with a named future reader stated, or remove it - and a reader outside the analysis counts.
decisions.status_source: Re-homed 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 specification-completion pass): CLAUDE.md's 'Fact-publication corollary to #6/#7/#12' (ratified 2026-07-10, amended 2026-07-12 - publish EVIDENCE-class facts broadly, each carrying its establishment status) remains the standing corollary; the layer-facing rule is now stated in the cross-cutting analysis contracts. OPEN_ITEMS OI-237 closes on this move
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` fact-publication corollary, with its evidence named there: `cowork_siloed_facts_audit.md` found 17 instances of facts being re-derived rather than read. The 2026-07-12 amendment's own recorded reason is the user's: a visible spread of published evidence lets a future design RECOGNIZE facts it would never have thought to ask for.

decisions.title: Contextual inversion bonuses fire only for major and minor candidates
decisions.verbatim:
**Safety constraints (lesson from three-attempt history) — ⚠ SUPERSEDED BY ITER 46, see §4.1g.** As
originally written: bonuses never fire for Diminished, HalfDiminished, Augmented, or Suspended
candidates — only Major and Minor. The existing `inversionSuspicionMargin` /
decisions.plain: The bonuses that let a neighbouring chord tip an inversion reading were restricted to plain major and minor chords, after three earlier attempts without that restriction all made things worse.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2171-2179 records Iter 46 extending the same helpers to Augmented and HalfDiminished. The §4.1b statement carries no supersession note - see OPEN_ITEMS OI-236 ★ Verbatim RE-TAKEN 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 truth-sync): the §4.1b passage now carries the supersession note it lacked, and states the constraint that actually survives at HEAD, which differs between the two helper predicates (OPEN_ITEMS OI-236 discharged). The decision's own words are preserved in place, marked 'As originally written'.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1867-1867: recorded as a hard-won safety constraint, the lesson of a three-attempt history in which the bonuses fired on qualities they were not measured on.

decisions.title: Augmented and half-diminished candidates receive the inversion bonuses too (Iter 46)
decisions.verbatim:
Extending these gates put Augmented and
HalfDiminished inversion candidates on equal footing with Major/Minor.
decisions.plain: The restriction above was later relaxed for augmented and half-diminished chords, because without the bonuses their correct inverted readings never reached the shortlist at all. It was the single largest improvement of that iteration path.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:2169-2182 (Iter 46, commit 36bf4738a8)
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:2171-2179: keeping D-101's constraint made correct inverted readings unreachable, and extending the two helper predicates to augmented and half-diminished was 'the largest single improvement of iteration path 1'.

decisions.title: Pedal-point detection is a second pass, accepted only on two conditions
decisions.verbatim:
**Pass 2** is triggered only when the Pass 1 bass PC is NOT a chord tone of the
winner.
decisions.plain: When the lowest note does not belong to the chord the upper voices spell, the program re-analyses without it. It accepts that reading only if the upper voices give at least two different pitch names and the answer is clearly better than the next different-rooted one.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3882-3917 'Status: Implemented (Session 18, master fb9a27ce9a)'. Suspended on the record arm - see D-021. SUPERSEDED BY D-207 - open_items/OI-194.md:7 records the ratified successor (user, 2026-07-26): the voice-independent pedal-point class replaces this bass-only second pass and the `isPedalPoint`/`pedalBassPc` fact it produces
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:3891-3896: a single pass over an organ point either forces a bass-root reading and suppresses the upper-voice harmony, or returns a slash chord with the wrong root when a template accidentally fits. The 'different-root competitor' detail carries its own recorded reason at :3640-3643 - several templates share a root, so a gap measured against rank 2 collapses to about 0.047 and blocks detection for bare triads.

decisions.title: The bass-is-root bonus is conditioned on corroborating support
decisions.verbatim:
`bassNoteRootBonus` is now conditioned on corroborating root-position support in the
accumulated tones:
decisions.plain: Being the lowest note no longer counts as strong evidence of being the chord's root unless the chord above actually supports that reading. Without a third or fifth above it, the bonus almost vanishes.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:3662-3710; the failure it fixed is documented across four corpora at :3406-3419
decisions.rationale: Measurement, ARCHITECTURE.md:3667-3686: four corpora (Chopin mazurka, Mozart sonata, Corelli trio sonata, Beethoven quartet) were inspected at the score and found to share ONE mechanism - the bass moves faster than the harmonic rhythm, so each bass note independently takes the bonus and overrides the root the chord tones above already identify. The fix conditions the bonus on corroborating root-position support rather than shrinking it.

decisions.title: The spelling written in the score is read through ONE shared interpreter
decisions.verbatim:
read through the **shared** `engravingbridge::lineOfFifths` primitive (the Layer-1.5 spelling
  view) — one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy.
decisions.plain: How a note is spelt on the page - F sharp versus G flat - is interpreted in one shared place, not re-implemented by each stage that needs it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1368-1371. ARCHITECTURE.md:1379-1383 records the unification residual: the legacy scorer still carries its own second reader until the legacy path retires
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:1369-1371 - 'one interpreter, not a per-layer tpc copy' (#6): two interpreters of the notated spelling can disagree, and open_items/OI-173 records what that costs when it happens (four inequivalent definitions of the same predicate).

decisions.title: The augmented-sixth labels are gated to the Standard and Baroque presets
decisions.verbatim:
**Preset gating is NOT implemented — corrected 2026-08-02 (`OPEN_ITEMS.md` OI-112(c); this section
asserted "Gated to Standard and Baroque presets only", and the code defers exactly that).**
decisions.plain: The specific Italian, French and German augmented-sixth labels are shown only under the classical presets.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-112 already records this preset-gating as stale; open_items/OI-201 records that the record arm collapses the family to a plain major triad symbol ★ Verbatim RE-TAKEN 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 truth-sync): §5.11's assertion 'Gated to Standard and Baroque presets only' was corrected, since the formatter explicitly defers that gate for want of preset context (`chordsymbolformatter.cpp:882-883`) and emits the labels under every preset (OPEN_ITEMS OI-112(c) discharged). The decision's own words survive at the home, quoted inside the correction.

decisions.title: American English throughout
decisions.verbatim: All identifiers, comments, and documentation use American English spelling.
decisions.plain: Analyzer, not analyser; color, not colour.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:492-502; restated in CLAUDE.md Conventions
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:492-502: MuseScore's own codebase is American English, so one spelling convention throughout is what keeps identifiers matching across the boundary.

decisions.title: Cross-platform by default
decisions.verbatim:
All code must run on every platform officially supported by MuseScore Studio: Windows,
macOS, and Linux.
decisions.plain: Everything must work on Windows, macOS and Linux; platform-specific code is allowed only where unavoidable and must be walled off.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:676-682
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:676-682: the code must run on every platform MuseScore Studio officially supports, so platform-specific code is permitted only when unavoidable and must be abstracted so the rest of the module stays platform-agnostic.

decisions.title: The open-items register is the one home for every unresolved issue, and the index is the status of record
decisions.verbatim:
this file is the complete INDEX and
> the **authoritative status surface**
decisions.plain: Every known unresolved problem has exactly one row in one file, and that row - not the longer write-up beside it - is the official statement of where it stands.
decisions.status_source: OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-13; the standing rule is in CLAUDE.md 'The open-items register'
patterns: index row AND its detail file
decisions.rationale: Measurement, OPEN_ITEMS.md:3-5: the register was created after a full-repository sweep found 91 open items scattered across 12 tracking surfaces with 11 status contradictions.

decisions.title: The decisions register records what was decided and its status - nothing else
decisions.verbatim:
**The register holds WHAT WAS DECIDED, and its status. Nothing else.** The proposed
   `conformance` field is REMOVED.
decisions.plain: This decisions register says what was decided and whether it still stands. Whether the code obeys it is tracked separately, in the open-items register, because those two things change on different clocks.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67 (SHAPE RATIFIED, three rulings)
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:49-54 (the user's recorded rationale): a decision's status changes only when someone rules again, whereas whether the code obeys it changes every time the code moves. Holding both in one row produces a register that silently goes stale - the exact failure the issue register was created to end.

decisions.title: A decision belongs in the owning layer's specification; the register is an index
decisions.verbatim:
**A decision belongs, wherever possible, in the OWNING LAYER'S SPECIFICATION** — that layer's
   section of `ARCHITECTURE.md` — and the register is the **index and pointer**, never a
   substitute home.
decisions.plain: A decision about how a stage should work is written into that stage's part of the architecture document. This decisions register only points at it.
decisions.status_source: open_items/OI-208.md:46-67; follows the CLAUDE.md Conventions rule of 2026-07-28
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, open_items/OI-208.md:55-62: the layer specification is where a reader looks for how a layer should work, so a register that held the decision instead of pointing at it would become a second home (#6) and the specification would stay silent.

decisions.title: Never work from memory instead of documented facts
decisions.verbatim:
No assertion, design, decision, dispatch or report may rest on recalled or
  inferred content when a documented source exists. Open the primary source and cite it
  (file:line).
decisions.plain: If a document records something, read it and quote it rather than remembering it. Being right from memory does not count, because correct memory and incorrect memory look the same until you check.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; its founding instance is the Layer-2 note-collection reading that this adjudication's method is built to prevent
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, with its founding instance recorded there: correct memory is indistinguishable from incorrect memory without checking, and the check is what surfaces the parts the memory did not contain - on 2026-07-28 the Layer-2 specification turned out to state explicitly and twice what had been reported as ambiguous.

decisions.title: Music-theory words are reserved for their music-theory meaning
decisions.verbatim:
Any term that coincides even slightly with music theory is used
  ONLY in its musical sense.
decisions.plain: In this project a score is a piece of music, a key is a tonality, and a measure is a bar. Where a word is needed in its everyday computing sense, it must be qualified - candidate score, map key, measurement.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28; open_items/OI-229 records the convention STANDING for new writing and the tree-wide cleanup as an unratified future work item
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, `CLAUDE.md` Conventions, user-directed 2026-07-28: this is a music-analysis system, so an ambiguous domain vocabulary makes every document harder to read and every specification easier to misapply.

decisions.title: The decoder commits its best path; there is no abstention on the key axis
decisions.verbatim:
**(d) On the key axis the decoder commits its maximum-a-posteriori path; it never abstains.** The estimator
always names a key for every committed segment, so the abstention counter the regression stop reads is
decisions.plain: The joint estimator always names a key. It never declines to answer on the key axis, so the abstention counter is always zero.
decisions.status_source: Re-homed 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 specification-completion pass): formerly recorded only in the CLAUDE.md gate block (A), the OI-178 adoption baselines (user-ratified 2026-07-26). The tension with D-090 (calibrated abstention, ARCHITECTURE.md §5.7a) is NAMED at the new home and deliberately NOT resolved there - resolving it is later work. OPEN_ITEMS OI-237 closes on this move

decisions.title: The regression stop is the granularity-robust unit; root governs, key and Roman numeral ride beside
decisions.verbatim:
the **class-(b) (pitch-class-decidable-root) root-disagree DURATION
  must be NON-INCREASING** vs the committed reference — the *meaningful* functional errors never grow.
decisions.plain: A change is allowed to ship only if the total amount of music on which we name the wrong chord root - counted where the root is decidable at all - does not grow. The key and the Roman numeral are watched alongside but do not govern.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md gate block (A), ratified R10-b 2026-07-06; supersedes the batch case-identity stop preserved as block (C)
decisions.rationale: Measurement, `CLAUDE.md` gate block (C): the batch region gate it replaced under-counted the true per-onset root error by roughly 15 to 56 times - it measured a small music21-filtered corner in which pitch-class-undecidable rotations were about 53 % of the residual, against about 3.5 % on the robust unit - so the robust unit is governed by the meaningful errors and is segmentation-invariant by construction.

decisions.title: The system is a module inside MuseScore Studio, not a plugin
decisions.verbatim:
This system is implemented as a new module (`composing`) within MuseScore Studio's
existing C++ codebase. It is not a plugin. It integrates directly with MuseScore's
score model, rendering pipeline, playback engine, and UI infrastructure.
decisions.plain: The harmonic analysis is built into MuseScore Studio's own program code as a new component of it, not added on afterwards as a plugin. It uses MuseScore's own score model, engraving, playback and interface directly.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:422-426: the analysis library itself has NO engraving dependency and is pure music theory; the bridge layer is what touches the engraving model. Being a module rather than a plugin is what lets that bridge exist at all.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:374-378 (§1.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The long-term intent is an official contribution to MuseScore Studio
decisions.verbatim:
The long-term intent is for this to become an official contribution to MuseScore Studio.
All code follows MuseScore's coding standards, licensing requirements, and contribution
guidelines.
decisions.plain: The aim is for this work eventually to become part of MuseScore Studio proper, so it is written to MuseScore's own coding, licensing and contribution rules from the start.
decisions.rationale: Derivation not recorded for the intent itself. What the record does state is the consequence it carries (ARCHITECTURE.md:381-382): following MuseScore's standards from the start is what keeps the contribution possible.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:380-382 (§1.2); restated at ARCHITECTURE.md:6821-6823 (the composing module is 'intended as a future contribution'). ★ READ WITH the CLAUDE.md DISTRIBUTION CONSTRAINT (D-197): the MusicXML declared-mode import patch cfc7eb5e39 is FORK-LOCAL ONLY and must NEVER reach musescore/MuseScore. Two recorded positions - a general intent and a one-patch exception - and the record does not state how the general intent applies to the rest of the tree.

decisions.title: GPL v3, and every external library must be GPL v3 compatible
decisions.verbatim:
All code is licensed under **GPL v3** — consistent with MuseScore Studio's open source
license. All external libraries used must be GPL v3 compatible.
decisions.plain: All the code is released under the GPL v3 licence, the same licence MuseScore Studio uses, and no outside library may be used unless its licence is compatible with that.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:386-387: consistency with MuseScore Studio's own open source licence. A GPL-incompatible library would make the code undistributable with MuseScore.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:384-387 (§1.3). No date or ratifier stated. The per-file consequence is ARCHITECTURE.md:6654 - a GPL v3 header on every file.

decisions.title: The MuseScore contributor licence agreement is signed before any pull request
decisions.verbatim:
The Contributor License Agreement (CLA) with MuseScore must be signed before any
pull requests are submitted.
decisions.plain: Before any of this work is offered back to MuseScore as a pull request, the contributor agreement with MuseScore must be signed.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:389-390 (§1.3), restated at ARCHITECTURE.md:6750-6752 (§18.3). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: MuseScore's coding style is followed, with clang-format run before every commit
decisions.verbatim:
Follow MuseScore's existing coding style throughout:
- Formatting defined in `.clang-format` — run clang-format before every commit
- Naming conventions — consistent with existing MuseScore code
- File headers — GPL v3 license header on every file (see existing files for template)
- Include ordering — follow MuseScore's convention
decisions.plain: The code looks like MuseScore's own code: the formatter configuration in the repository is run before every commit, names follow MuseScore's conventions, every file carries the GPL v3 header, and includes are ordered MuseScore's way.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:519-523 (§2.8): read how MuseScore already does a thing and follow the same pattern rather than inventing parallel infrastructure - the same reason that governs panels, score traversal, playback, settings and localization.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6649-6655 (§17.1). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Where MuseScore's documentation practice is minimal, the higher standard applies
decisions.verbatim: Where MuseScore's documentation practice is minimal, use good practice instead.
decisions.plain: Following MuseScore's conventions does not mean copying how little it documents. Where MuseScore documents sparsely, this project documents properly instead.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6709-6712 (§17.3): the analyzers are the most complex components in the codebase, and a musician with reasonable theoretical knowledge must be able to read them and understand why each decision was made.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6649-6657 (§17.1). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every public class and method is documented in musical terms
decisions.verbatim:
Every public class must have a documentation comment explaining:
- What musical concept it implements
- What it receives as input (in musical terms)
- What it produces as output (in musical terms)
- What it does not handle (important for setting expectations)
decisions.plain: A public class must say which musical idea it implements, what music it takes in, what it produces, and what it deliberately does not handle. A public method must say the same about the musical operation it performs, in musical terms rather than programming terms.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:504-508 (§2.6) with :6322-6323: the documentation is written so a person with reasonable musical knowledge and basic programming familiarity can read it, including MuseScore contributors with no familiarity with this codebase at all.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6659-6671 (§17.2). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: public class must have a documentation comment

decisions.title: Every non-obvious scoring weight or threshold explains its musical reasoning
decisions.verbatim: Every non-obvious scoring weight or threshold must explain its musical reasoning.
decisions.plain: A number in the scoring code that is not self-evident must be accompanied by the musical reason it has the value it has.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6709-6712 (§17.3): the analyzers are the most complex components, and their weights and thresholds are where the musical judgment actually lives - an undocumented one is unreadable and unarguable.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6673 (§17.2). No date or ratifier stated. ★ This is the rule the 2026-08-01 CLAUDE.md Conventions entry generalizes from scoring values to design decisions as a class (D-195) - and the rule this register's rationale field serves.

decisions.title: The analyzer code must be readable by a musician
decisions.verbatim:
Every scoring weight, threshold, and heuristic must be documented with its musical
rationale. A musician with reasonable theoretical knowledge must be able to read the
analyzer code and understand why each decision was made.
decisions.plain: Every weight, threshold and rule of thumb in the chord and key analyzers carries its musical reason, to the standard that a musician with ordinary theoretical training can read the code and see why each choice was made.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6709: these are the most complex components in the codebase, so they are where readability is worth the most.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6707-6719 (§17.3), which gives a worked example from existing code (the circle-of-fifths interval deltas). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every test documents the musical situation, the expected result, and what a failure means
decisions.verbatim:
Every test must document:
- What musical situation is being tested
- What the expected result is and why it is musically correct
- What a failure would indicate about the system's behavior
decisions.plain: A test says which musical situation it exercises, what the right answer is and why it is musically right, and what it would mean about the system if the test failed.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6728-6729: the tests must be readable by MuseScore contributors with no deep familiarity with this codebase.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6721-6729 (§17.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One coherent piece of functionality per pull request
decisions.verbatim:
Each pull request should implement one coherent piece of functionality. Large
pull requests are hard to review. The phased plan in Section 15 defines natural
PR boundaries.
decisions.plain: Each contribution offered back to MuseScore does one thing.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6744-6746: large pull requests are hard to review, and the phased plan defines where the natural boundaries fall.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6742-6746 (§18.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: An architectural decision that changes is documented in the same commit
decisions.verbatim:
When an architectural decision changes — update this document in the same commit.
Stale documentation is worse than no documentation because it actively misleads.
Claude Code should update relevant sections of this document as its last act when
a session changes an architectural decision.
decisions.plain: When a design decision changes, the change to this document goes in the same commit as the change to the code.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6757: stale documentation is worse than no documentation, because it actively misleads.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6754-6759 (§18.4); the standing principle is CLAUDE.md #10 (D-174). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: update this document in the same commit

decisions.title: Styles are defined entirely in data; adding one never requires code changes
decisions.verbatim:
Musical styles are defined entirely in JSON files. The C++ code implements mechanisms —
voice leading optimization, chord generation, voicing rules — while JSON files define
parameters. Adding a new style never requires C++ changes.
decisions.plain: A musical style is a data file. The program code implements the mechanisms - voice leading, chord generation, voicing - and the style file supplies the numbers that make one style behave differently from another. Adding a style is never a code change.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:440-442 (§2.1) with the worked wrong/correct pair at :392-402: behaviour that branched on a style's identity would make every new or renamed style a code change.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4292-4296 (§6.1); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: styles are defined entirely in JSON

decisions.title: Style conflicts resolve by a declared priority - explicit overrides always win
decisions.verbatim:
**Conflict resolution priority:**
1. System defaults — lowest priority
2. Mixin sources — in declared order, later overrides earlier
3. Explicit `overrides` in the style file — highest priority, always wins
decisions.plain: When a style assembles itself from several inherited sources, the order of precedence is fixed: system defaults are weakest, inherited sources come next in the order they are declared with later ones winning, and anything the style file states explicitly wins outright.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4338-4341 (§6.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The style loader never names a style in code
decisions.verbatim:
The style loader scans the styles directory recursively and loads all valid JSON files.
It never references specific style IDs in code — it simply loads whatever it finds.
decisions.plain: The loader reads whatever style files it finds in the styles directory. No style's name appears anywhere in the program code.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:487-490 (§2.4): no comparison against a style name anywhere in the codebase - style-specific behaviour flows entirely through parameters.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4372-4375 (§6.4); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1/§2.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One shared style taxonomy, not two parallel vocabularies
decisions.verbatim:
The style vocabulary the presets select on is **one shared, hierarchical taxonomy** (common-practice / jazz / vernacular
families — Baroque, Classical/galant, Romantic; trad, swing/songbook, bebop, hard-bop, cool, modal; blues, ragtime,
gospel-soul, rock, pop, folk, barbershop) — the **same** set the Harmonic Vocabulary (§7) tags its entries with, not two
parallel vocabularies. Inclusion rule: a style is listed iff it has a **distinct functional-harmonic vocabulary** (free
jazz / atonal excluded).
decisions.plain: The list of style families the presets choose from is the SAME list the harmonic vocabulary tags its entries with - one hierarchy, not two that can drift apart. A style earns a place on it only if its functional harmony is genuinely distinct, which is why free jazz and atonal music are not on it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4422-4424 - #6, one path per concern, applied to a vocabulary: two parallel taxonomies of the same thing would diverge, and the inclusion rule (a distinct functional-harmonic vocabulary) is what keeps the list from growing by analogy.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4418-4428 (§6.7); full proposal `cowork_progression_schema_dictionary.md` §6/§12 and `cowork_style_clustering_plan.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The style taxonomy is a theory-based first version; grounding it empirically is committed work
decisions.verbatim:
It is a **theory-based v1**; **empirically grounding** it — deriving the clusters *and* the
per-style weights by clustering corpora — is committed future work (`cowork_style_clustering_plan.md`)
decisions.plain: The style families and their weights are currently drawn from music theory, not from data. Deriving both from corpora instead is recorded as work that will be done, not as an option.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4425-4427: the clusters and their feature distributions are one data-derived object, and it is reachable for jazz and pop from lead-sheet corpora even where note-level ground truth is scarce - which is what makes the grounding committable rather than aspirational.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4418-4428 (§6.7). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmonic vocabulary is a queried reference component, not a layer of the analysis
decisions.verbatim:
It is reference knowledge **queried** by the layers and by
future tools, **not a pipeline layer**. Entries carry **provenance** (established theory), not a ground-truth-validation
status — validation is the *consumer's* concern (verifiability contract, §2.15).
decisions.plain: The catalogue of progressions and substitutions is something the analysis stages ask questions of, not a stage they pass through. Its entries say where the theory comes from; whether that theory holds up against real music is the caller's question, not the catalogue's.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4446 - the verifiability contract (D-029): reference knowledge grounded in established theory may be carried without corpus validation, provided the consumer that puts it under load is the one that must validate it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4437-4451 (§7); own specification `cowork_progression_schema_dictionary.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A voicing type is never requested directly; the style selects it
decisions.verbatim:
// Style determines which voicing types are used and in what proportion.
    // Never call with a specific voicing type directly — encode that in the style.
decisions.plain: A caller asking for a voicing says which style it wants, never which voicing technique. The style decides whether the answer is a drop-2, a shell, a chorale spacing or something else, and in what proportion.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4555-4558: keeping the interface voicing-type agnostic is what lets a new voicing type be added as a generator implementation plus a style parameter, without the interface changing.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4550-4572 (§8.2); the principle it realizes is D-070 (§2.1). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: never call with a specific voicing type

decisions.title: A fixed element is a hard constraint the optimizer may never modify
decisions.verbatim:
Fixed elements are hard constraints in the voice leading optimizer — they anchor
the dynamic programming search. The optimizer guarantees never modifying them.
decisions.plain: Anything the user has pinned - a note, a voice, a chord, a passage - anchors the search for good voice leading. The optimizer works around it and never changes it.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4694-4733 (§9.1-§9.2). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: hard constraints in the voice leading optimizer

decisions.title: The inference demo view is a developer tool and is not shipped
decisions.verbatim:
A step-through visualization of the inference pipeline, for use by developers
during quality assurance and algorithmic development. Not shipped to end users.
decisions.plain: The step-by-step view of the analysis making its decisions exists so a developer can watch and judge it by eye and ear. It is not part of what a user gets.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4751-4753: it exists to make musical correctness checkable by eye and ear rather than only through the automated agreement numbers.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4745-4835 (§10.0), whose own status line reads 'Not yet started'. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmony maps are our own visual design, and are chosen partly to avoid intellectual-property claims
decisions.verbatim:
MTH Pro-style map based on Berklee chord-scale theory (Nettles, Levine). Positions
chords by functional region (tonic, subdominant, dominant) and shows available
tensions. Our own visual design — not a reproduction of MTH Pro's specific layout.
decisions.plain: The planned map of harmonic function draws on published chord-scale theory but is laid out our own way, not copied from the commercial product that inspired it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4888 and :4573: the circle of fifths and the Tonnetz were chosen partly because they carry no intellectual-property claim - the Tonnetz being a nineteenth-century mathematical structure - and the same reasoning is what forces an original layout for the functional map.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4885-4908 (§10.2-§10.4), all three marked planned. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: not a reproduction of MTH Pro

decisions.title: Chord preview uses MuseScore's note-input pathway, not the playback pipeline
decisions.verbatim:
**Implementation note:** Use MuseScore's note-input preview pathway (same as hearing
a note when clicking in input mode) — not the full score playback pipeline. The
full pipeline has too much latency for interactive map exploration. Inference runs
on a background thread via `QtConcurrent` to keep the UI responsive.
decisions.plain: Clicking a chord on a harmony map plays it through the same quick path MuseScore uses when you hear a note as you enter it, not through full score playback.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4938-4940: the full playback pipeline has too much delay for interactive exploration, and the inference runs on a background thread so the interface stays responsive.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4910-4940 (§10.5), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language model holds no object references - every tool call carries its own musical address
decisions.verbatim:
**Stateless tool-call model.** The LLM does not hold object references. Each
tool call carries its own musical address. No proxy objects, no EID handles,
no lifecycle management. This is the right model for LLM interaction and the
simpler one to implement.
decisions.plain: When a language model asks the program to do something, it names the place in the music each time. It never holds a handle to an object in the score.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6789-6790: no proxy objects, no element handles and no lifecycle management - recorded as both the right model for this kind of interaction and the simpler one to implement.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6780-6790 (§19.2), a planned module; full design `docs/llm_integration.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language model is a search agent and is never given the whole score
decisions.verbatim:
**LLM as search agent.** The LLM is never given a full score dump. It has
search tools (`find_notes`, `get_part`, `get_measure`, `search_harmony`) and
fetches what it needs iteratively — exactly as Claude Code uses Grep and Read
in a large codebase. Serialization quality is the critical foundation: clean,
hierarchical, beat-aligned, free of layout noise.
decisions.plain: Rather than being handed the entire score, the language model is given tools to find what it needs and fetches it piece by piece - the way a person reads a large document by searching it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6795-6796: because the model reads what it fetches, the quality of that serialization - clean, hierarchical, beat-aligned, free of layout noise - is the critical foundation.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6780-6796 (§19.2), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: never given a full score dump

decisions.title: The language model sees what the user set, not what the engraving engine derived
decisions.verbatim:
**Intentional vs. computed.** The LLM sees everything the user deliberately
set (pitch, dynamics, articulation, note color, lyrics formatting, visibility).
It does not see what the engraving engine derived (positions, beam geometry,
stem lengths, `LayoutData`). The `Pid` property system is the practical
boundary.
decisions.plain: The model is shown the composer's own choices - pitches, dynamics, articulation, colour, lyrics, visibility - and not the results of laying the music out, such as positions, beam geometry or stem lengths.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6802: MuseScore's own property system is the practical boundary between the two, so the split is enforceable rather than judged case by case.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6780-6802 (§19.2), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: does not see what the engraving engine derived

decisions.title: The composing module is the language model's context provider; the model never re-derives harmony
decisions.verbatim:
The composing module (`src/composing/`) is the LLM's context provider. Its
harmonic analysis output (chord symbols, Roman numerals, key inference,
harmonic rhythm) is included in every score section sent to the LLM. The LLM
does not re-derive harmony from raw pitch data — it receives pre-digested
musical context.
decisions.plain: Every stretch of music sent to a language model arrives with our harmonic analysis already attached - chord symbols, Roman numerals, key, harmonic rhythm. The model reads that; it does not work the harmony out from the notes itself.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6817-6819: the same analysis also drives the validation step that checks voice leading and harmonic consistency before a generated change reaches the score, so one analysis serves both directions.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6809-6823 (§19.3), a planned module. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The language-model bridge is built as a module but confined to the core access layer, so it can become a plugin
decisions.verbatim:
**Build strategy:** Implement the LLM bridge as a native module initially for
speed, but strictly constrained to the Core Access Layer only (never bypassing
it to the DOM). When the plugin API matures, migration to a plugin is then
straightforward. See `docs/llm_integration.md §11` for the full argument.
decisions.plain: It is written inside the program for speed of development, but restricted to the same narrow interface a plugin would have, so that moving it out to a plugin later is straightforward.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6825-6830: with a properly designed plugin interface the bridge does not need to live in the core at all - it becomes optional, independently updatable, provider-agnostic and open to community alternatives - so the constraint is what keeps that end state reachable.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6825-6835 (§19.4), a planned module; full argument `docs/llm_integration.md` §11. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Percussion is excluded from analysis and tuning; fixed-pitch instruments are the tuning anchor
decisions.verbatim:
Percussion instruments are excluded from both harmonic analysis and intonation.
Fixed-pitch instruments (piano) serve as intonation anchors when present.
decisions.plain: Unpitched percussion takes no part in working out the harmony and receives no tuning adjustment. Where a piano or organ is playing, the other instruments tune to it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4976-4977 and :4781-4782: a fixed-pitch instrument cannot adjust, so it is the natural reference - and its presence resets accumulated drift at every chord it plays.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4970-4990 (§11.2). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: One preference chooses the tuning system, and no tuning code hardcodes one
decisions.verbatim:
All tuning code paths read the preference at call time via `preferredTuningSystem()`
(defined in `notationtuningbridge.cpp`), which resolves the key through
`TuningRegistry::byKey()` with a `JustIntonation` fallback if the key is unset or
unknown.  No tuning code hardcodes a specific system.
decisions.plain: Which tuning system is in force is a single user setting, read afresh each time any tuning happens. No part of the tuning code has a system built into it.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:4992-5000 - #6, one path per concern: the same preference governs per-note tuning, chord-staff population and region tuning, so the three cannot silently disagree about what tuning the user asked for.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:4992-5008 (§11.2a). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A tie chain is one indivisible tuning event, and its tuning comes from one authority note
decisions.verbatim:
**Tied notes:** A non-partial tie chain explicitly carries a compositional instruction of
continuity. For region tuning, the entire non-partial tie chain is treated as one tuning
event. The chain must not be split. Its tuning is set from a single authority note and
protected thereafter; later harmonic regions tune around that established pitch.
decisions.plain: Notes joined by ties are one sustained sound, so they are tuned once and never split apart. The tuning is worked out from a single note in the chain - the one carrying a tuning anchor if there is one, otherwise the first - and applied unchanged to the whole chain.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5251-5252 and :4923-4924: a tie is a compositional instruction of continuity, so splitting it would contradict what the composer wrote; a user who wants the sustained sound retuned as the harmony moves writes a slur instead.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5251-5264 (§11.3c), with the region-tuning consequence at :5726-5729 (§11.6). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: A slur, not a tie, joins the halves of a split note
decisions.verbatim:
A **slur** (not a tie) connects the two halves.  This is a deliberate choice:
MuseScore's playback engine treats tied notes as one continuous sound with a single
tuning value, so a tie would silently discard note_B's tuning.  A slur produces two
independent playback events with legato articulation, allowing each half to carry
its own tuning offset.
decisions.plain: When a sustained note must be retuned partway through, it is cut in two and the halves are joined with a slur rather than a tie.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5691-5694: MuseScore's playback treats tied notes as one continuous sound with a single tuning value, so a tie would silently discard the second half's tuning; a slur produces two independent playback events, each able to carry its own offset.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5683-5694 (§11.4). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The split is visible in the score; the invisible alternative is deferred
decisions.verbatim:
The split is **visible** — the score shows two shorter notes connected by a slur.
This is the simplest correct approach and is fully undoable via MuseScore's standard
undo system.
decisions.plain: The reader sees two shorter notes joined by a slur where a note was retuned. The alternative - keeping the written note and hiding a silent playing copy - was designed and set aside.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5697-5698: the visible split is the simplest correct approach and is fully undoable through MuseScore's own undo. The excluded alternative's recorded blocker (:5360-5363) is that it needs a visual indicator for tuning-applied notes before it is practical.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5696-5703 (§11.4), with the deferred alternative recorded at `backlog_invisible_split.md`. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Only visible, sounding notes enter the pitch-class collection
decisions.verbatim:
Chord analysis filters notes with `visible = true` and `play = true`, excluding
both silent notes and any future invisible tuning artifacts from the pitch-class
collection.
decisions.plain: Notes marked invisible, and notes that do not play, take no part in identifying the chord - which also keeps any hidden note created by the tuning machinery out of the analysis.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5721-5722: the filter excludes both silent notes and any future invisible tuning artifact, so tuning a passage cannot change what the analysis of that passage sees.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5718-5722 (§11.4). No date or ratifier stated. The joint estimator's own eligibility flags are the Layer-1 fact surface (D-039/D-045).

decisions.title: The chord staff is the output, never an input to the analysis that fills it
decisions.verbatim:
The target staff is excluded from the analysis input — it is the output, not a
source.  This prevents feedback loops when re-running the analysis.
decisions.plain: When the harmonic reduction is written onto a staff, that staff's own contents are kept out of the analysis that produced them.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5787: it prevents a feedback loop when the analysis is re-run over music that already carries its own reduction. The joint estimator's record path realizes the same rule at its own input surface - D-013, open_items/OI-204.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5777-5787 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: target staff is excluded from the analysis input

decisions.title: Populating the chord staff overwrites whatever is in the selected range
decisions.verbatim:
**Any existing content in the selected region is overwritten.**  Re-analysis after
score edits simply selects the same range and runs again.  If the user wants to
preserve a previous analysis, they can undo or copy it elsewhere first.
decisions.plain: Running the reduction again over the same passage replaces what is there. Keeping an earlier analysis is the user's job - undo it, or copy it somewhere else first.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5789-5791 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: existing content in the selected region is overwritten

decisions.title: Roman numerals and Nashville numbers are never shown together on one staff
decisions.verbatim:
**Chord function notation** attached below the treble staff — either
`HarmonyType::ROMAN` (Roman numerals) or `HarmonyType::NASHVILLE` (Nashville
numbers), selected by the "Chord function notation" preference (None / Roman
numerals / Nashville numbers).  Roman and Nashville are mutually exclusive on
the staff because they encode identical information; displaying both would be
redundant and legibility-destroying.
decisions.plain: The chord staff shows one or the other beneath the music, chosen by preference, never both.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:5854-5856: the two notations encode identical information, so showing both would be redundant and would destroy legibility.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:5851-5856 (§11.5); the same choice on the analysis side is D-086. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Interactive annotations are written in the score's normal colour; the batch pipeline writes red
decisions.verbatim:
Interactive annotate path (human use): annotations written in score default
color (black). Publication-ready, indistinguishable from manually entered
symbols. No user preference exposed.

Automated pipeline (`batch_analyze` headless): annotations written in red,
hardcoded in `tools/batch_analyze.cpp`. Never exposed to human user. Used by
`auto_review.py` to filter our inferred annotations from pre-existing score
content by color comparison.
decisions.plain: When a person runs the annotation, what it writes looks like anything else they typed. When the headless batch tool runs it, everything it writes is red.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6043-6049: the interactive output is meant to be publication-ready and indistinguishable from hand-entered symbols, while the red is a filter criterion that lets the automated review separate our inferred annotations from whatever the score already contained.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6040-6049 (§11.5). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: New panels use MuseScore's own panel and interface infrastructure
decisions.verbatim:
New panels follow MuseScore's existing panel architecture — KDDockWidgets for
panel management, QML for UI components. Do not create parallel infrastructure.
Read how existing MuseScore panels are implemented before creating new ones.
decisions.plain: Any new panel is built with the same window-docking and interface technology MuseScore already uses, after reading how MuseScore's existing panels are built. No parallel machinery is created.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:519-523 (§2.8): read how MuseScore already does it and follow the same pattern - the same rule that governs score traversal, playback, settings and localization.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6158-6162 (§12.1); the panels themselves are planned (§12.2-§12.5). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every user-visible string goes through MuseScore's localization, in English and Swedish
decisions.verbatim:
All user-visible strings use MuseScore's existing Qt localization infrastructure
(`.ts` files, Qt Linguist). English and Swedish translations provided for all new strings.
decisions.plain: Text a user can read is translatable through MuseScore's own translation system, and every new string is supplied in English and Swedish.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6164-6165 (§12.1); listed in the Core scope at ARCHITECTURE.md:6617-6618. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Accessibility follows MuseScore's existing patterns
decisions.verbatim:
Accessibility follows MuseScore's existing Qt accessibility patterns — focus
management, keyboard navigation, screen reader hooks.
decisions.plain: Keyboard navigation, focus handling and screen-reader support are done the way MuseScore already does them.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6167-6168 (§12.1); listed in the Core scope at ARCHITECTURE.md:6618. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The harmonic-display preference exists for clarity, not for cost
decisions.verbatim:
A user preference controls whether harmonic analysis is shown in the status bar. This
preference exists for UI clarity — some users find the chord and key information
distracting, particularly when doing work unrelated to harmony.
decisions.plain: The setting that hides the harmonic information from the status bar is there because some users find it distracting, not because the analysis is expensive. Switching it off does not skip the analysis.
decisions.rationale: Measurement named in the record, ARCHITECTURE.md:6174-6174: the analysis cost at this seam is 'well under 1ms'. ★ That number is the LEGACY bounded-window path's; open_items/OI-203 and OI-206 record the record arm running a whole-score decode per selection, measured in seconds on large scores - so the reason this preference is not a performance control no longer holds as stated.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6170-6199 (§12.1a). No date or ratifier stated. ★ Verbatim RE-TAKEN 2026-08-02 (the phase-1 truth-sync): the paragraph's second half — 'It is not a performance control: analysis cost is negligible (well under 1ms) and suppressing the display does not require skipping the analysis' — is FALSE at HEAD on both clauses and is corrected in place (OPEN_ITEMS OI-242 discharged). The surviving quote is the decision proper: the preference exists for clarity. Whether it should also become a performance control is left OPEN at the home, not decided.

decisions.title: Our data lives in separate files inside the score archive; the score file is never touched
decisions.verbatim:
MuseScore's MSCZ format is a ZIP archive. Our metadata lives as additional files
within the archive alongside `score.mscx`:
decisions.plain: Constraints, branches, cached analysis and preferences travel with the score as extra files inside its archive, beside the standard MuseScore score file, which our code never modifies.
decisions.rationale: Stated trade-off, ARCHITECTURE.md:6290-6294: the score stays a valid standard MuseScore file with zero interference in MuseScore's own reading and writing, and our data travels with it. The accepted cost is stated too - exporting to MusicXML, PDF or MIDI loses it, which is acceptable because the workflow is MuseScore-native.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6276-6294 (§13.1), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Every custom file carries a format version, and the score file is never rewritten by our persistence
decisions.verbatim:
All our custom files include a format version field. When the format changes,
migration code handles existing files. The score.mscx is never modified by our
persistence layer.
decisions.plain: Each of our own files records which version of its format it is, so older files can be migrated when the format changes; the standard MuseScore score file inside the archive is never rewritten by us.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6296-6300 (§13.2), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Arranger interactions are logged from the start, with consent, as future training data
decisions.verbatim:
The system logs arranger interactions from the start — with user consent — as
future ML training data. Every suggestion accepted, modified, or rejected is a
labeled training example specific to vocal jazz arranging, filling the corpus gap
identified in the design phase.
decisions.plain: Every suggestion a user accepts, changes or rejects is recorded - with their consent - as a labelled example for future machine learning.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6343-6344: the recording exists to fill the corpus gap identified in the design phase, there being no existing labelled corpus of vocal jazz arranging decisions.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6339-6356 (§14.2), a planned component. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: Chord symbols already in a score are a second analyst's opinion, not ground truth
decisions.verbatim:
Mode 2 — Pre-existing symbols present: treated as a second analyst's opinion,
not ground truth. Judge comments on agreements and disagreements without
scoring disagreements as errors. Framing: "two analysts may reach different
but equally valid conclusions."
decisions.plain: When the automated review meets a score that already carries chord symbols, it treats them as another analyst's reading. Disagreements are discussed, not scored as our errors.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6375-6376, in the record's own words: two analysts may reach different but equally valid conclusions. Errors are scored only in Mode 3, against a known ground-truth corpus (:5989-5990) - the same distinction the project's standing rule draws between corroboration and ground truth.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6358-6383 (§14, the automated annotation review), marked planned. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: The development tools are not part of the shipping product
decisions.verbatim:
The following tools live in `tools/` and are **not part of the shipping product**.
They are compiled/run only in development builds (`MUE_BUILD_ENGRAVING_DEVTOOLS=ON`).
decisions.plain: The batch analysis tool, the comparison scripts and the remaining measurement tools are built only in development builds and never ship to a user.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6419-6422 (§15). No date or ratifier stated.
patterns: not part of the shipping product

decisions.title: The batch tool deliberately skips post-load layout
decisions.verbatim:
and `iex_musicxml` — no notation module required. Because the tool only consumes
logical score structure, it deliberately skips forced post-load layout; this avoids
legacy native MSCX cache-overflow crashes (for example Mozart `K533-3`) without
changing the emitted harmonic-analysis JSON.
decisions.plain: The headless analysis tool never lays the music out on the page, because it only ever reads the logical structure.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, ARCHITECTURE.md:6431-6433: skipping the layout avoids a legacy cache overflow crash on some scores (Mozart K533-3 is named) without changing the harmonic-analysis output at all.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6424-6433 (§15). No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: What is out of scope, and what degrades gracefully at the boundary
decisions.verbatim:
Live and real-time operation, film synchronization, adaptive game music, non-Western
traditions (graceful degradation at boundary), post-tonal and serial music (graceful
degradation at boundary), audio transcription from recording, spatial music, extended
techniques as primary language.
decisions.plain: Live performance, film and game synchronization, audio transcription, spatial music and extended techniques as a primary language are not attempted. Non-Western traditions and post-tonal music are not attempted either, but the system is required to fail gracefully where it meets them rather than producing confident nonsense.
decisions.status_source: ARCHITECTURE.md:6594-6643 (§16), which sorts the whole feature set into Core / Important / Prepared / Out of scope. No date or ratifier stated.

decisions.title: #1 - build only on established fact and theory
decisions.verbatim:
1. **Fact- and theory-based coding only.** Build only on established fact and theory —
   published research, public algorithms, public software. Fact-finding (investigative)
   coding is allowed.
decisions.plain: Nothing is built on a hunch. Every method comes from published research, a public algorithm, or public software. Investigating to find out what the facts are is a separate, permitted activity.
decisions.rationale: Derivation not recorded as a separate defense - this is the founding premise the other principles are stated against. Its operational consequence is recorded: #3 makes an unexpected finding a failure of this principle rather than a curiosity (CLAUDE.md:14-16).
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:9-11, the user's standing list. CLAUDE.md:120-132 records the provenance of the whole list: principles 1-11 are the user's standing list; #12-#16 were ratified by the user 2026-07-06; #17-#19 and the surprise-scope rule 2026-07-10; #20-#24 and the constrained-optimum ledger corollary 2026-07-18 at the joint-estimator plan review.

decisions.title: #2 - target the specific open question, not the general topic
decisions.verbatim:
2. **Specific research over general.** Most research so far has been general or on
   already-handled topics; target the specific open question.
decisions.plain: Research effort goes to the exact question in front of us, not to the surrounding subject generally or to something already handled.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:12-13: most research done so far has been general or on already-handled topics - the observation that motivates the rule.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:12-13, the user's standing list. CLAUDE.md:120-132 records the provenance of the whole list: principles 1-11 are the user's standing list; #12-#16 were ratified by the user 2026-07-06; #17-#19 and the surprise-scope rule 2026-07-10; #20-#24 and the constrained-optimum ledger corollary 2026-07-18 at the joint-estimator plan review.

decisions.title: #3 - an unexpected finding is a failure to diagnose, not a curiosity
decisions.verbatim:
3. **An unexpected finding means we have failed #1** (and possibly #2, #4, #6). Surprise
   signals that the fact/theory basis was incomplete — treat it as a failure to diagnose,
   not a curiosity.
decisions.plain: Being surprised means the facts and theory we built on were incomplete. Surprise is treated as a defect in our own understanding, not as an interesting result.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:14-15: surprise signals that the fact and theory basis was incomplete, which is a failure of #1. Its operational form is #13 - surface it as a stop before building around it.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:14-16, the user's standing list. CLAUDE.md:120-132 records the provenance of the whole list: principles 1-11 are the user's standing list; #12-#16 were ratified by the user 2026-07-06; #17-#19 and the surprise-scope rule 2026-07-10; #20-#24 and the constrained-optimum ledger corollary 2026-07-18 at the joint-estimator plan review.
patterns: unexpected finding means we have failed

decisions.title: #4 - the long-term goal is maximum-precision inference
decisions.verbatim: 4. **Long-term goal: maximum-precision inference.**
decisions.plain: The objective the whole project is measured against is getting the analysis as accurate as it can be made.
decisions.rationale: Derivation not recorded - this is the stated objective, not a decision derived from something else. It is what the decision-neutrality corollary (CLAUDE.md:106-118) means by 'the ultimate objective'.
decisions.status_source: CLAUDE.md:17, the user's standing list. CLAUDE.md:120-132 records the provenance of the whole list: principles 1-11 are the user's standing list; #12-#16 were ratified by the user 2026-07-06; #17-#19 and the surprise-scope rule 2026-07-10; #20-#24 and the constrained-optimum ledger corollary 2026-07-18 at the joint-estimator plan review.

decisions.title: #5 - when facts may be scarce, investigate
decisions.verbatim:
5. **Investigate when facts may be scarce.** If we are unsure whether facts are scarce,
   gather more facts.
decisions.plain: If it is unclear whether we know enough about something, the answer is to go and find out, not to proceed on what we have.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:85-89 (the scope-of-surprise rule): explorational runs whose purpose is to eliminate ignorance are exactly where surprises are permitted - so fact-finding is the cheap stage that keeps surprises out of the expensive one.

decisions.title: #6 - total unification: one path per concern
decisions.verbatim: 6. **Total unification — no duplication of any code.** One path per concern.
decisions.plain: There is exactly one implementation of any given concern. No duplicated code, no second place the same question is answered.
decisions.rationale: Measurement named elsewhere in the record: `cowork_siloed_facts_audit.md` found 17 instances of facts being re-derived rather than read (CLAUDE.md:94-95), and open_items/OI-173 records four inequivalent definitions of one predicate as the cost of a second path. The end-state reading is fixed by #23 and by the decision-neutrality corollary (CLAUDE.md:116-118): #6 is a structural end-state principle, not a preservation claim for whatever exists now.

decisions.title: #7 - a layer is enhanced only with what belongs to it
decisions.verbatim:
7. **Adhere to layers.** Enhance a layer only with algorithms/methods that belong to it,
   nothing else. Worst case, this forces a layer redesign rather than a cross-layer patch.
decisions.plain: A stage of the analysis gets only the methods that are properly its own. If the right method does not belong there, the layers are redesigned rather than the method smuggled across.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:22: the worst case is a layer redesign, which is explicitly preferred to a cross-layer patch.

decisions.title: #8 - no inference-problem-driven coding until every method sits in its correct layer
decisions.verbatim:
8. **No inference-problem-driven coding until all methods and algorithms are implemented
   in their correct layer.**
decisions.plain: Work is not steered by whichever analysis error is currently visible. Until the structure is built out, a fix is made at the stage that owns it, at the time that stage is being built.
decisions.rationale: Derivation not recorded as a separate defense. The related recorded position is that a fix at its #8-correct stage is 'never a knob-turn' - the phrase carried on the open-item rows that defer a fix for this reason (for example open_items/OI-192, OI-216, OI-217).

decisions.title: #13 - surface a surprise as a stop before building around it
decisions.verbatim: 13. **Surface a surprise as a STOP before building around it** (the operational form of #3).
decisions.plain: When something unexpected turns up, work halts and it is reported. It is never quietly worked around.
decisions.rationale: Stated constraint, CLAUDE.md:31: this is the operational form of #3 - if surprise means the fact basis was incomplete, then building on top of the surprise builds on the same incomplete basis.
